findings.title: Deduplicate concurrent builds for the same index key
findings.body: Protecting only the final cache assignment allows GetIndex to return a cache miss throughout an in-progress build. Two first searches for the same NamespacedResource can therefore build separate indexes and unconditionally overwrite each other in the cache. If one finishes and receives a watch update before the other publishes its older snapshot, that update is lost from subsequent searches. Keep the cache-miss/build path single-flight per key while allowing different keys to build concurrently.

findings.title: Synchronize TotalDocs with background cache writes
findings.body: This new log evaluates TotalDocs after starting the write-event consumer. Bleve's TotalDocs iterates its cache map without acquiring cacheMu, while the consumer can build an index for a previously uncached namespace and insert it into that map. With writes arriving during startup, counting documents can therefore race with cache insertion and crash the process with concurrent map iteration and map write. Protect cache enumeration with the read lock, or obtain the count before starting the consumer.

findings.title: Preserve the stopped-state check when removing lazy initialization
findings.body: The removed per-request Init calls also checked initErr, which Stop sets to reject requests while stopping or stopped. Eager initialization does not replace that lifecycle guard. The SQL backend's Stop only cancels its pollers and leaves the database usable, so Create, Update, and Delete now continue accepting writes after Stop even though watch delivery has stopped; IsHealthy can also continue reporting SERVING. Retain a separate lifecycle-state check on requests.

findings.title: Unwind initialized resources when constructor initialization fails
findings.body: The constructor now returns nil on an Init failure without cancelling or stopping work that Init already started. For example, search initialization can successfully start its SQL event poller, then initWatcher can fail on the second WatchWriteEvents database query. The caller receives no server handle with which to call Stop, leaving the first poller and initialized lifecycle resources running. Unwind successfully initialized components on this error path, including the search watcher that uses a detached background context.
